:::{#rem-half-space-sides}
#### The two sides of a hyperplane

Every point of $\reals^p$ is in exactly one of $\mathcal{H}^+$, $\mathcal{H}$ and $\mathcal{H}^-$,
because the number $\dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} + b$ is positive, zero or negative.
The vector $\vec{w}$ points into $\mathcal{H}^+$:
the number $\dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} + b$ goes up when $\vx$ moves in the direction $\vec{w}$.

:::
